atoms.span: UbuWeb is a digital library of freely downloadable avant-garde art, film, music as well as visual, concrete and sound poetry.
is a free, ad-free digital library and online archive for avant-garde art, film, music, and poetry.
Audio & Music: Features mp3 archives, sound art, early internet audio, and curated collections like The 365 Days Project and Tellus Audio Cassette Magazine.
Mission: To provide open, web-based educational access to obscure, out-of-print, and marginalized avant-garde materials.
Operations: Built on a gift economy model, running with no budget, zero registration, and server/bandwidth support donated by universities.

mt: 'UBUWEB' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE ARCHIVE AT ITS GRAIN, ITS 2024 PAUSE AND 2025 RETURN EXACT; ITS COUNTS ON NO SAVED PAGE; ITS TERMS OF HOLDING (RIGHTS WITH THEIR HOLDERS, REMOVAL ON THE ARTIST'S REQUEST) NOT CARRIED
d: THE ARCHIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'UbuWeb is a free, ad-free digital library and online archive for avant-garde art, film, music, and poetry.' Overview & History (founded 1996 by Kenneth Goldsmith; mission; 'gift economy model, running with no budget'; status, 'Active'); Scope & Contents ('over 7,500 artists', 'more than 2,500 full-length avant-garde and experimental films and videos'; audio; poetry and /ubu Editions; papers). Four cards: Wikipedia, the Poetry Foundation, Arte Útil, Instagram; no card from ubu.com.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the name, the Overview gives the archive's history, mission, way of running and present status, then its contents by section.
findings: HISTORY AND STATUS EXACT. 'The site paused in January 2024 (declaring itself complete), but resumed operations in February 2025 in response to global political changes.' The saved Wikipedia article: 'In January 2024, UbuWeb announced it was no longer active' and 'In February 2025 the site resumed its activities, citing the "political changes in America and elsewhere around the world" as a reason to be active again.' The founding ('1996 by poet Kenneth Goldsmith') matches the article and the FAQ ('founded in November of 1996, initially as a repository for visual, concrete and, later, sound poetry'). The volunteer editors are on the Poetry Foundation card only ('volunteer-run').

THE COUNTS AND THE BUDGET. 'over 7,500 artists' and 'more than 2,500 full-length avant-garde and experimental films and videos' are in none of the three saved pages. 'running with no budget' rounds the FAQ: 'UbuWeb has no need for funding. All work is done solely on a volunteer basis. Our only cost is our monthly hosting fee, which amounts to US$50 each month.' The 'gift economy' is the article's ('It remains non-commercial and operates on a gift economy').

THE TERMS OF HOLDING NOT CARRIED. The composition says nothing of rights. The FAQ: 'The copyrights belong to the copyright holders, not us.'; 'If it's out of print, we feel it's fair game.'; 'should an artist find their material posted on UbuWeb without permission and wants it removed, please let us know.' The census row reads these as UbuWeb's standing with the maker, whose one recorded act is the request for removal; the composition's 'Mission' ('open, web-based educational access to obscure, out-of-print, and marginalized avant-garde materials') keeps the out-of-print half of the policy and drops the holder and the artist. The Library of Congress archiving on the home page ('The site is permanently archived by the United States Library of Congress.') is not carried.
analysis: The archive composed accurately at its grain, with its pause and return exact and two counts on no saved page. The terms on which it holds others' work, rights left with their holders and a work withdrawn at its artist's request, are absent.
per_note: Kenneth Goldsmith named as founder; no institution named (the donors are 'universities'); sources carded, none from ubu.com.

evidence.record_quote: Founded in 1996, UbuWeb is the internet's largest archive of free avant-garde materials.

atoms.reference: A completely independent site run on a volunteer basis by editors across the United States; created by the poet Kenneth Goldsmith, named its editor.

evidence.record_quote: UbuWeb has no need for funding. All work is done solely on a volunteer basis. Our only cost is our monthly hosting fee, which amounts to US$50 each month.
No. UbuWeb is a completely independent site. However, several universities and partners have generously offered us server space and bandwith, with no restrictions or input regarding our content.
Our editors are pretty much spread across the United States: New York City, Utah, California, etc.
The site was created by poet Kenneth Goldsmith in 1996
UbuWeb was founded in November of 1996, initially as a repository for visual, concrete and, later, sound poetry. Over the years, UbuWeb has embraced all forms of the avant-garde and beyond.

It houses and distributes freely the entire archive of the Tellus Audio Cassette Magazine project.
Beyond its repository of works, UbuWeb features curated sections including /ubu Editions book-length editions of contemporary poetry , selected and introduced by the poet Brian Kim Stefans .

atoms.reference: A distribution center for hard-to-find, out-of-print and obscure materials, transferred digitally to the web.

atoms.reference: Nothing for sale, commercial-free; copyrights belong to the copyright holders; out-of-print works posted, in-print works left alone, a work removed when it returns to print or its artist asks.

evidence.record_quote: Nothing is for sale on UbuWeb. It's all free.
UbuWeb is completely commercial-free and it will always stay that way.
The copyrights belong to the copyright holders, not us. You'll need to seek them out for proper permission.

If it's out of print, we feel it's fair game. Or if something is in print, yet absurdly priced or insanely hard to procure, we'll take a chance on it. But if it's in print and available to all, we won't touch it.
Should something return to print, we will remove it from our site immediately. Also, should an artist find their material posted on UbuWeb without permission and wants it removed, please let us know.
